editorial.headline: Wholesale Automotive Parts: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet a Bali-wide PMA moratorium blocks registration there today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this wholesale automotive-parts activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the national position is open. The activity itself is the wholesale trade of new and used motor-car spare parts, components, equipment and accessories, including tyres, as well as automotive batteries and accumulators. It is a supply-chain classification: the business is concerned with wholesale distribution of the parts and accessories that keep cars supplied and maintained.

The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the classification is defined by what is traded—automotive parts, components, equipment, accessories, batteries and accumulators—rather than by a narrow company-size profile. A business operating at any of those listed scales can fall within the activity where its commercial function is wholesale trade in those goods.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Read on its own terms, that is a fully open national foreign-investment position: the foreign stake is not capped below full ownership. But the national reading is not the final answer for a Bali registration. The location-specific restriction in the record changes the result decisively.

Bali records the activity as Blocked (risk class). At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, and Bali’s May 2026 moratorium blocks PMA registration on that basis. The stated provincial rule is island-wide and permanent: it blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. So the honest picture is not a qualified version of national openness. Nationally, this activity is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, PMA registration is blocked under the provincial moratorium. That conclusion concerns the PMA registration position specified in the record, and it is the condition an investor must take seriously before treating the national ceiling as an available Bali entry route.
